proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Quasi-finiteness propagates from the finite source-fibre of u to every object u_j isomorphic to u and to every arrow between them: the source fibre points are isolated in the fibre of R over p, the flat locally finitely presented target map of fibres is open, and the scheme-theoretic source fibres are finite over their residue fields by the two-fibres lemma applied within the orbit. The technical etale splitting lemma for quasi-finite parts, applied to the two pairs of structure morphisms with the orbit point sets, produces the etale neighbourhood with residue field identification and the open and closed decompositions of the base changes into finite pieces U' and R' plus complements, giving conclusions (a) through (d) and the fibre level versions of (e) and (f). Zariski shrinking by removing closed images of the open and closed complements upgrades (e) and (f) to global inclusions, also for the unit and inverse maps, and the groupoid axioms of the restricted structure are inherited from the full base change, giving (g). (source lines 2447-2561)

core_obligations: Write the source fibre of u as the finite set of arrows r_1 to r_n (assumption 6). By finite-fibre (02NG) the map s is quasi-finite at each r_i, by composition-quasi-finite (01TL) so is the composite to S, and by the isolation characterization (01TH) each r_i is isolated in the fibre of R over p (proof lines 2448-2456). Flatness and finite presentation of t pass to the fibres (01U9, 01TS), hence the target map of fibres is open (01UA), so the finitely many images u_j are isolated in the fibre of U over p and the structure morphism is quasi-finite there (proof lines 2457-2470). The scheme-theoretic fibre F_u is finite over the residue field of u (03JA); the two-fibres lemma identifies F_u and F_{u_j} over a common field extension, so each F_{u_j} is finite over the residue field of u_j and the source fibre of each u_j is finite; assumptions (2) and (6) hold at every u_j, and repeating the first paragraph gives quasi-finiteness of s at every point of the set of all arrows r_1 to r_N between orbit objects, with the set-theoretic bookkeeping under t, the projections of the composition preimage, the unit and the inverse recorded for the orbit (proof lines 2472-2503). The technical splitting lemma (02LN) applied to the two pairs produces the etale neighbourhood (S', p') with residue field identification and decompositions of the base changes into finite pieces with bijective fibres over the orbit sets, giving (a), (b), (c), (d) and the fibre level inclusions of (e) and (f) (proof lines 2505-2527). Each complement preimage such as the preimage of W under the source map of R' is open and closed in a scheme finite over S' and avoids the fibre over p', so shrinking S' by the closed image empties it; iterating for the target, the composition, the unit and the inverse upgrades (e) and (f) to global inclusions (proof lines 2529-2550). The restricted structure on the pieces is then a groupoid over S' because its axioms hold for the full base change groupoid, giving (g) (proof lines 2552-2561).
proof_roadmap: Propagate quasi-finiteness and isolation from the source fibre of u to the whole orbit through the open flat target map of fibres (proof lines 2448-2470).
Use the two-fibres lemma to extend fibre finiteness to every orbit object and record the set-theoretic orbit bookkeeping (proof lines 2472-2503).
Apply the technical etale splitting lemma to both structure morphisms to obtain the decompositions and conclusions (a) through (d) (proof lines 2505-2527).
Shrink the neighbourhood by closed images of open and closed complements to globalize (e) and (f), also for unit and inverse (proof lines 2529-2550).
Conclude (g): the restricted structure is a groupoid over S' by axiom inheritance (proof lines 2552-2561).
